subject: POC network access and MAP finalization
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@auroramed.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps for POC environment (MAP items)

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. Procurement asked me to confirm the exact technical items Redwood needs to get the POC environment stood up so they can align internal approvals. To keep us on the MAP timeline, can you confirm the following:

- The API key generation process and whether keys will be scoped to a single org/project.
- Any org-level setup you need from our side (owner email, billing contact).
- IP ranges you need added to our allowlist and the preferred timing for the change window.
- VPC peering requirements and whether you need a shared subnet or route tables pre-configured.

We're targeting a 2-week evaluation window and procurement needs the cost/commitment summary for the MAP package. If possible, send a one-page checklist and the technical template we should hand to our infra team.

Appreciate the help — happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if that speeds things up.

Best,
Alex Li
Senior Product Manager
AuroraMed

--
Attachment: auroramed_poc_request.pdf (pdf stub)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@auroramed.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for POC environment (MAP items)

Hi Alex,

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I've attached a one-page MAP checklist and a VPC peering template that your infra team can drop into their ticketing system. High-level answers below and next actions:

- API keys: We'll generate an API key tied to a Redwood org ID. For the POC we recommend a single scoped key per environment (staging/poc) with read/write token limits. We can rotate keys on request; there is also an option to use a per-user API key for auditing.
- Org setup: Please provide the preferred org owner email and billing contact. We will create the Redwood org and share the org ID and an admin invite.
- IP allowlist: Please add outbound ranges for our serving control plane and inbound ranges for the VPC connector. Suggested CIDRs are in the attached auroramed_poc_ips.csv. If you need a smaller set, we can offer an ephemeral tunneling option during the POC.
- VPC peering: We support AWS VPC peering and GCP VPC peering. The template includes the route table changes we expect. For peering we need the account ID, VPC ID, and a maintenance window to establish routes (expected 30-60 min).

Next steps (action items):
1) Aurora -> share org owner email, billing contact, and preferred peering window (2 business days recommended).
2) Aurora infra -> confirm IP allowlist entries (CSV attached).
3) Redwood -> we will provision the POC org, generate the initial API key, and send the admin invite once we have the org owner email.

I've looped in our solutions engineer and SRE to handle the peering work.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_map_checklist.pdf, vpc_peering_template.txt, auroramed_poc_ips.csv

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: AuroraMed POC — tech handoff and schedule

Team,

Forwarding AuroraMed's request and the MAP items they confirmed. Proposed timeline: provision org + API key on Friday 5/21, VPC peering on Monday 5/24 (maintenance window 10:00-11:00 PT), start traffic tests on 5/25.

Please see task split below:
- dev_patel: provision POC org, create scoped API key, enable logging and token limits. Post the API key in the secure token vault and share with Laura for delivery.
- vivek_kulkarni: review the auroramed_poc_ips.csv and confirm the minimal set we need for the peering config; validate the vpc_peering_template against their AWS account ID (they listed it in their ticket).
- marissa_cole: CS lead — coordinate on onboarding docs, acceptance criteria, and the eval plan (2-week objectives + success metrics).

Important: use the standardized MAP checklist and record the HubSpot timeline (HS-48279). Keep the config immutable once we start traffic tests to ensure repeatable metrics.

On Fri I'll generate the initial API key after dev confirms provisioning is complete. Reply-all with any blockers.

Thanks,
Laura

Laura,

Thanks for the checklist and the quick coordination. Confirming the items below so we can close the MAP and move to procurement:

- Org owner: alex.li@auroramed.com
- Billing contact: procurement@auroramed.com
- IP allowlist: I've attached the trimmed CSV with our approved CIDRs (see auroramed_poc_ips.csv). We approved the minimal set (5 entries).
- VPC peering: window confirmed for Mon 5/24 10:00-11:00 PT. AWS account ID: 123456789012, VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h.
- Procurement: PO attached (auroramed_po_48279.pdf) — legal will sign once we receive the final MAP summary and the invoice.

Question: for API keys, do you generate the key and provide it via the secure vault, or should we create a service account on our side and request key exchange? We prefer Redwood to generate and rotate the initial key.

If we get those final bits today, procurement can finish approvals and we can hit the MAP start date of 5/25.

Alex
